bibliographic.title: Thermal expansion of FeWO₄ (Ferberite) and FeWO4:Fe2WO6 (7:1): a comparative X-ray and neutron diffraction study

bibliographic.abstract: The thermal expansion of natural FeWO4 (ferberite) and synthetic FeWO4:Fe2WO6 (7:1) was investigated over the 2–1123 K temperature range combining single-crystal and powder X- ray diffraction together with neutron powder diffraction. High-precision lattice parameters were obtained for both samples. The temperature dependence of the unit-cell volume was analysed using physically based thermodynamic models, including the Kroll and Berman approaches as implemented in EoSFit7. All datasets are well reproduced within their respective temperature intervals. However, significant differences are observed between the behavior of ferberite and FeWO4:Fe2WO6, which has a ~40% smaller thermal expansion coefficient and a reduced reference volume. Possible origins, including microstructural and phase-coexistence effects, are discussed. The results provide a comprehensive description of the thermal expansion behavior of FeWO₄ across a wide temperature range.

samples.sample_description: Natural FeWO4 single crystals obtained from the Monte Cambillaya mining district, La Paz, Bolivia, ground to prepare polycrystalline samples.
Synthetic polycrystalline two-phase mixture of FeWO4 (ca. 88%) and Fe2WO6 (ca. 12%) prepared by co-precipitation.

datasets.dataset_description: Temperature-dependent single-crystal diffraction data collected on a Bruker D8 diffractometer using silver radiation between 40 and 500 K.
X-ray diffraction measurements performed on an X'Pert diffractometer using Cu Kα radiation in the temperature ranges 15–300 K and 298–1123 K.
Neutron powder diffraction data collected on the D20 diffractometer using a germanium monochromator in the temperature range 2–500 K.
